notes: A directory entry's size and sha256 are its root block's: the bytes a gateway returns for /ipfs/<cid>?format=raw. The DAG under each root is exported as the CAR in cars[] (path, size, sha256), which is not a separately pinned object.
No origins are listed: no candidate-operated node serves these blocks. Filebase (the upload) and Pinata (the second pin) are pinning vendors; their gateway URLs are locators, never identities.

The second pin is missing: Pinata did not pin baguqeerahe3ecgiyigcgdg6gmxqsmc5ylzlucf4kb3n5xcqi5tvtiebpv2ta, baguqeeram5hefoyihxelublnx3hzdmbdxg5gavyukspzevkwnii7b5zexipq (outcomes verbatim in pins[]); Filebase is the only provider pinning these roots.
The manifest does not list itself; its CID is recorded in the run record.
Consumers read the global elephant-atlas IPNS; this pilot has no Atlas PR, so no IPNS name or index CID applies to it.
